parameters.content:
## Webhook URLs

Use separate webhooks for batch CSV and chat UI.

Batch CSV / Slack-style batch:
`/webhook/reha-contentops-batch`

Chat UI:
`/webhook/reha-contentops-chat`

Backend URL is hardcoded in the HTTP Request nodes for n8n Docker:
`http://host.docker.internal:8000/process-feedback-batch`.

The batch lane accepts multipart form uploads with `file=@...` and returns an ops summary JSON. The chat lane returns a short `{ reply: ... }` JSON for the browser UI.

## Reha ContentOps AI Showcase

This workflow intentionally keeps AI logic in the FastAPI backend.

Batch lane:
Manual/Webhook -> backend batch API -> ops summary -> review queue, content-gap ticket, ops digest

Chat lane:
Chat webhook -> backend batch API -> ops summary -> chat reply

Backend owns:
- exercise database loading
- classification
- metadata extraction
- matching
- content-gap detection
- output CSV generation

n8n only orchestrates, formats payloads, and routes outputs.

## Replace these payload nodes with real integrations

- Review Queue Payload -> Slack / Google Sheet / Notion
- Content Gap Ticket Payload -> Jira / Linear / Asana
- Ops Digest Payload -> Slack digest or email

The payloads are intentionally explicit so the workflow demos cleanly without credentials.

## Two Demo Lanes

Batch lane:
- Manual Demo Trigger
- Incoming Slack Batch Webhook
- Normalize Webhook Batch
- Call Backend Batch API
- Build Ops Summary
- Review Queue Payload
- Content Gap Ticket Payload
- Ops Digest Payload

Chat lane:
- Incoming Chat UI Webhook
- Normalize Chat Message
- Call Backend Batch API (Chat)
- Build Ops Summary (Chat)
- Build Chat UI Reply
- Respond to Chat UI

Both lanes call the same FastAPI backend. The chat lane also mirrors the review/gap/digest payloads for showcase visibility.
